page: Microsoft Azure F16as_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and running under Microsoft Hyper-V, it provides 16 dedicated physical cores with a 1:1 core-to-thread ratio. The configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware cache structures include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Modern vector and machine learning instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AVX-512 BF16, and AVX VNNI are supported alongside cryptographic extensions like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

This instance type does not bundle any local ephemeral storage, requiring remote storage solutions such as Azure Premium Storage for persistent file systems. Similarly, it lacks discrete GPU acceleration and does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Dedicated physical cores deliver strong determinism by eliminating hyper-threading resource contention, though storage-intensive workloads must rely entirely on remote network-attached disks.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional single-threaded compute efficiency. In stress-ng single-core tests, the F16as_v7 achieved 3623.09, ranking in the top 10%. It demonstrated similarly high tier performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 40.97 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 17.16 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is solid, recording 57891.85 on stress-ng multi-core and 237.33 GB/sec on multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. In lightweight AI evaluation, text generation using a small 135M parameter LLM achieved top-tier throughput of 409.71 tokens/sec, while prompt processing reached 3167.25 tokens/sec.

Memory and general system throughput reflect middle-tier performance profiles. The instance demonstrated 103.87 GB/sec for large-block read-only memory bandwidth and 68.94 GB/sec for large-block writes. Standard service tests registered 46.4 million operations/sec for Redis SET workloads and 32.04 GB/sec for static web serving. The balanced allocation of 4 GB RAM per physical core makes the F16as_v7 cost-effective for CPU-bound computation, batch data compression, CPU-based lightweight machine learning inference, and high-throughput application logic.
